raw.title: Toggl: Senior Full Stack
raw.description:
Headquarters: Tallinn, Estonia
URL: https://toggl.com/jobs/

We are looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join one of our Product Tribes, the cross-functional units that own the end-to-end experience for a specific Toggl user role. You'll join the Tribe building for managers, the people who plan work, protect margins, and keep projects on time and on budget.

You own significant parts of that experience end-to-end, working hands-on with product and design to ship work that matters. You'll do this as we build and launch Toggl 2.0, our consolidated planning, time tracking, and time intelligence product.

The salary for this position is €83,000 annually.

You can work from anywhere in the world as long as your main location is between UTC-4 and UTC+4.

 

The Role

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end, from the data model and the API to the interface someone actually clicks: the technical approach, the quality of what ships, and whether it actually works for the people using it. You are accountable not for tickets closed, but for clarity, craft, and outcomes.

You'll work in the Tribe serving managers, across planning and capacity management, dashboards, and billable work. This is some of the most data-dense, interaction-heavy surface area in the product: schedules and capacity views, reports, and visualizations that have to stay fast and readable at real customer scale. The interesting problems live on both sides of the API here - the query behind a capacity view matters as much as how that view renders. You'll build with React and TypeScript on the frontend and our backend services (mostly Golang) and data layer (Postgres) behind them, alongside a product manager, a designer, and engineers who are used to owning their work and pushing back when something isn't right. In a tribe of 5 other engineers, your impact and visibility are high.

Our team meetings are scheduled between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC. Your availability and commitment to participate in these sessions are essential for effective collaboration and team alignment.

Your main responsibilities will be:

Ownership and delivery

  • Take projects from problem to production. Own the technical approach for major features front to back, break the work down sensibly, sequence it, and ship in slices rather than one big drop.

  • Make the technical calls in your area. Choose between options, name the tradeoffs, and decide without waiting for permission or escalating routine judgment.

  • Keep your work visible without being chased. Flag risks and slips early, keep the Tribe in the loop, and unblock yourself.

Craft and quality across the stack

  • Build interfaces people trust with dense, real-world data. Planning views, dashboards, and reports that stay fast, accessible, and readable when the dataset gets ugly.

  • Design the data and API layer those views depend on. Model it so the feature you're building now doesn't make the next three harder.

  • Own performance as a feature, end to end. Profile, measure, and fix the slow query and the slow render instead of hoping the data stays small.

  • Write code others can work in. Sensible components and services, real test coverage where it earns its keep, and a codebase that's easier to change after you touch it.

Working with product and design

  • Shape solutions, don't just implement them. Push on the problem, question requirements that don't hold up, and propose simpler paths when you see one.

  • Partner closely with design. Prototype early, spot the edge cases in a flow before it's built, and hold the bar on UX quality with your designer rather than after handoff.

  • Stay close to users and evidence. Join user tests, read the feedback, look at the data, and let it change what you build.

Raising the bar

  • Review code with intent. Give precise, actionable feedback that makes the change and the person better.

  • Mentor and interview. Help other engineers grow, and help us hire well.

  • Improve things across team boundaries. Spot shared components and duplicated work between Tribes, and raise it before we build the same thing twice.

AI as core leverage

  • Use AI tools extensively in your daily work for exploration, prototyping, code generation and review, debugging, research, and writing. AI fluency is not optional. It's part of how you increase your speed, depth, and impact - and you're expected to help the rest of the Tribe get better at it too.

 

About You

You will thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience building and shipping production web applications end to end, and can lead major projects rather than just contribute to them.

  • Are genuinely comfortable on both sides of the stack. You're deep on one side and properly capable on the other, not someone who hands off at the API boundary.

  • Have deep, practical knowledge of JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and modern CSS - including state management and side-effect handling in large applications.

  • Are solid on backend fundamentals: at least one backend language you know well, API design, relational data modelling, and enough instinct for query performance to spot the problem before production does. Prior Golang experience is not mandatory but you have to be willing to adopt it and become comfortable with it fast.

  • Hold an extremely high bar for quality. You know what great looks like, you notice the details others miss, and you don't ship work you wouldn't put your name on.

  • Have a knack for data-heavy product surfaces - performance, readability, and the principles behind a chart that actually communicates something.

  • Care about the user's problem, not just the ticket. You start from what someone is trying to get done and work back to the implementation.

  • Own outcomes, not output. You follow your work into production, watch how it behaves, and fix what needs fixing.

  • Thrive in ambiguity and move fast. You make confident decisions with incomplete information, adapt when things change, and course-correct without drama.

  • Are hands-on with AI tools. You actively use AI as a core part of how you build, not a side experiment, and you have opinions about where it helps and where it doesn't.

  • Don't need to be managed. You set your own direction, keep people in the loop, and ask for help when it matters.

  • Have excellent written and verbal English communication skills. You write clearly, explain technical tradeoffs to non-engineers without jargon, and default to async communication that others can follow.

  • Are eager to contribute to the engineering team's growth - code review, mentoring, and interviewing included.

  • Value transparency, ownership, and speed over perfection. You ship, learn, and improve rather than waiting for the perfect plan.

  • Nice to have:

    • Experience with TanStack is a bonus, and so is a real understanding of frontend caching and eventual consistency, we'd love to hire someone who's dealt with that tradeoff directly.

    • Experience with capacity planning, scheduling, reporting, or other complex B2B SaaS products.

    • Experience working with distributed or microservice systems, a basic understanding of infrastructure and infrastructure as code, and some experience creating, improving, or debugging CI/CD pipelines.

This Role Is NOT

  • A ticket-taker role. If you want fully specced work handed to you, this isn't the right fit.

  • A pixel-pusher translating finished designs into code with no say in the problem or the solution.

  • A role where you hand off at the API boundary. If "that's a backend ticket" is your instinct, this will frustrate you.

  • A role where quality is someone else's job. Toggl doesn't have a dedicated QA
    team or layer: there's no separate team that will catch your bugs, write your
    tests, or own your performance regressions.

  • A place to work in isolation from users. You'll be expected to know who you're building for and why.

  • A role for people who need heavy process, frequent approvals, or top-down direction to do their best work.

 

The Team

We are a global team of ~80 awesome people working from over 40 countries around the globe. We hire globally, you work locally—in the heart of London, a beach outside of Río de Janeiro, or a quiet village near Florence, the choice is yours. Every few months we travel to meet up somewhere in the world and spend some quality time together. We place a huge amount of trust in our people, and we measure the outcomes rather than the work itself. Our values fuel our results.

What's Happening at Toggl

Toggl is at an exciting turning point. We're taking our best-in-class time tracking - trusted and loved by millions of users worldwide - and expanding it into something bigger: Toggl 2.0. One product that brings together time tracking, planning, capacity management, reporting, and insight. The idea is simple: better time tracking creates better data, which powers everything else. We call it time intelligence. We build with AI throughout, and we think it's a real multiplier for strong engineers rather than a substitute for them. The judgment, the tradeoffs, and the accountability for what ships stay with people.

 

Benefits

  • Freedom to choose when and how much you work—we only measure results

  • 24 days of paid time off a year, plus your local holidays

  • Unlimited sick leave

  • In-person meetups for team-building (expenses covered)

  • 4-6 weeks paid sabbatical (depending on tenure)

  • Laptop budget up to 2,500€ and it renews every 3 years

  • €2,000 budget to set up your home office and an additional €300 every year after 3 years of tenure

  • €3,000 per year for co-working space membership and/or internet service at home

  • €4,000 per year contribution to use for training, workshops, and conferences

  • €2,400 per year contribution for any equipment or services to improve and/or maintain your physical and mental health

  • Support for buying tools you need for doing your best work (even eyeglasses if you need a new pair)

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/toggl-senior-full-stack

While a traditional allogeneic stem cell transplant has been the best hope for many, the transplant itself can prove fatal or lead to serious conditions, such as graft vs. host disease. Orca Bio is a commercial-stage biotechnology company redefining the transplant process by developing next-generation cell therapies with the goal of providing significantly better survival rates with dramatically fewer risks. With our purified, high-precision cell therapies we hope to not only replace patients' blood and immune systems with healthy ones, but also restore their lives. The Senior Specialist, Global QMS will help implement Orca Bioâs global quality management system across all sites. This role will support and lead the internal audit program, supplier management program, and inspection readiness. This role will support the growth and expansion of the global quality program to support manufacturing of our cell therapy products. You will help establish, implement and maintain the audit program across Orca Bio sites to ensure compliance with GxP and regulatory expectations. Your role will support Orca Bios commercial readiness and ongoing clinical programs by managing and facilitating audits, resolving supplier-related quality issues and interacting with quality management teams at the site levels to ensure consistent application of quality systems across the organization. 
 Responsibilities: Plan, schedule and execute internal audits across all sites and functions in accordance with the internal audit program. Develop audit agenda, conduct interviews, review processes and generate audit reports. Support the global Quality Management Review (QMR) process, ensuring timely data collection, analysis, and reporting to senior leadership. Support the supplier qualification and management program, including risk assessments, supplier audits, and ongoing monitoring to ensure compliance with GxP requirements. Drive global inspection management activities, ensuring cross-functional and site readiness for FDA, EMA, and other health authority inspections. Provide oversight and guidance to site QMR administrators ensuring consistent quality system implementation across all Orca Bio sites. Establish and monitor global QMS key performance indicators (KPIs), oversee trending of quality metrics, and ensure data-driven insights are used to improve quality systems and performance. Partner with IT and business process owners to identify and implement QMS system enhancements, including defining requirements, driving prioritization and ensuring changes are validated and compliant. Review, approve, and provide quality oversight for validation documentation (e.g., equipment qualification, computer system validation, process validation) for global enterprise systems (e.g. MasterControl, ERP systems, Trackwise, etc.) ensuring alignment with regulatory and internal requirements. Collaborate with cross-functional and site leadership teams to drive continuous improvement initiatives, ensuring the QMS evolves in line with business needs and regulatory expectations. Experience: Bachelorâs degree in a scientific or engineering discipline required; advanced degree preferred. Minimum 5+ years of relevant Quality Assurance or Quality Systems experience in a GxP-regulated environment, with at least 2-3 years in a leadership role. Strong knowledge of global quality regulations and standards (FDA, EMA, ICH, ISO 9001, 21 CFR Parts 210/211/820, EU GMP). Proven experience leading Quality Management Review, internal audit programs, supplier management processes, and validation oversight. Demonstrated success in establishing and trending quality performance metrics and KPIs. Experience supporting and/or administering electronic QMS systems and partnering with IT for system enhancements. Experience working in a multi-site or global quality organization strongly preferred. Excellent organizational, analytical, and communication skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across functional and site boundaries. 
 $90,000 - $120,000 a year 
 The anticipated annual salary range for this job is based on prior experience in the role/industry, education, location, internal equity, and other job-related factors as permitted by law. For remote-based positions, this range may vary based on your local market. Full-time employment positions will also be eligible to receive pre-IPO equity and annual bonus, in addition to competitive medical, dental, and vision benefits, PTO, 401(k) plan, life and accidental death and disability coverage, and parental leave benefits. Other perks include subsidized daily lunches and snacks at our on-site locations. Who we are We are driven by a passion for science and compassion for patients. We act with urgency to ensure our treatments are one day accessible to all who need them. We live by our core values of passion, courage, and integrity. Excellence in our work means the chance to unlock a better quality of life for our patients, and with that comes tremendous responsibility. We innovate on a path that hasnât been paved. We embrace an entrepreneurial spirit and take calculated risks to achieve our mission. We arenât afraid to ask âwhy notâ and challenge the status quo. We maintain a start-up culture of camaraderie and leadership by example, regardless of title. Weâre proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and recognize that celebrating our differences creates stronger, lasting solutions that better serve our team, our patients and their healthcare providers. title: Team Lead Education
description: **This position is based in Germany with hybrid or remote working options. Applicants must hold a valid work/residence permit for the respective location.** Chaos is a leading global software company that provides world-class visualization and design solutions, empowering creative minds to bring ideas to life. For over twenty years, Chaos has developed innovative technologies serving multiple industries, including architecture and design, media and entertainment, and product e-commerce. Chaosâ solutions help architects, designers, VFX artists/animators, and other creative professionals share ideas, optimize workflows, and create immersive experiences. Headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, Chaos is a global company with offices in 11 cities worldwide. In 2022, Chaos and Enscape merged, bringing together two industry-leading companies into one. Since then, Chaos has continued to grow with the additions of Cylindo, AXYZ Design, and Evolve Lab, further expanding our expertise and solutions across architecture, design, e-commerce, and AI. For more information, please visit chaos.com . Role Overview The Team Lead, Education Sales leads the Education sales team and owns the end-to-end go-to-market strategy for the Education segment, covering both University and Student markets. The role is responsible for driving new institution and student customer acquisition, growing ARR within the existing base, and reducing churn across both segments. The University segment operates through direct, relationship-led sales to institutions, while the Student segment runs as a low-touch, digital-first purchase journey, requiring close partnership with the Ecommerce team to optimise the online funnel, conversion rates, and pricing experience. Reporting to the Sr. Director GTM Strategy & Transformation, this role requires a commercially driven sales leader with a hands-on approach, a track record of owning segment revenue end-to-end, and the ability to coach and develop a team while remaining personally active in deals. The role operates with a high degree of autonomy and suits someone who wants to build and scale a team rather than maintain one. Main Responsibilities Lead and develop the Education sales team, setting clear individual performance expectations, coaching from the front, and stepping into deals directly where needed to support pipeline and attainment targets. Own and scale a proactive, discovery-led outbound motion to win new institution and student customers, continuously refining outreach cadence and qualification criteria. Drive expansion and retention within the existing student and institution customer base, identifying and executing initiatives that grow ARR and reduce churn. Own ARR and pipeline growth within the University segment through relationship-led, direct sales to institutions, tracking key performance metrics and diagnosing and correcting underperformance. Own ARR and seat growth within the Student segment, which runs as a low-touch, digital-first purchase journey rather than a traditional sales motion; partner with the Ecommerce team to continuously optimize the online funnel, conversion rates, and pricing experience. Own accurate pipeline forecasting and attainment reporting for the Education business, providing reliable visibility into performance for sales reviews and senior leadership. Partner with RevOps, Marketing, Product, and Ecommerce to ensure Education-specific campaigns, content, and product feedback are prioritised and executed effectively. Required Experience At least 5 years of sales experience within a SaaS or technology environment, including demonstrated experience leading a sales team with direct accountability for team performance and revenue outcomes. Proven track record of owning a direct sales territory or segment end-to-end, from pipeline generation through closed, retained revenue. Experience managing and influencing a low-touch, digital or ecommerce-led purchase journey (funnel, conversion, pricing) is a strong advantage. Previous experience in Architecture, Education, EdTech, or a related vertical is an advantage, but not required. Required Skills Takes full ownership of commercial outcomes: builds pipeline, closes deals, and drives team performance without waiting to be directed. Leads by example in the field: comfortable coaching team members through live deals and personally engaging in high-priority opportunities where it makes a difference. Translates ARR and revenue data into clear, defensible strategy, is able to identify where performance is off track, diagnose the root cause, and act on it. Communicates with credibility at senior level: presents team results, forecasts, and strategic needs clearly to VP-level and cross-functional stakeholders. Able to build effective working relationships and collaborate cross-functionally across Ecommerce, RevOps, and Marketing: driving digital funnel and conversion improvements for the Student segment without direct authority. Operates effectively with high autonomy in a fast-moving environment: sets own priorities, creates momentum without close direction, and holds a consistently high personal bar for execution and results. Familiarity with MEDDICC or a similar sales qualification framework is an advantage. We welcome people who value teamwork, stick to their commitments and are curious to explore new ways for achieving mastery. If you believe that you are a good match for the job, just send us your CV in English . Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Confidentiality of all applications is assured. An NREC developer can go from developing mapping for a mining robot operating in extreme environments (https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/solutions/mining/profiler.html) to developing hardware and controls for unique research vehicles (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-URxpqi0oAU). Another may go from developing training products for humanitarian workers (https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/solutions/defense/other-projects...) on to assistive technologies that make work easier for farmers around the world (https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/solutions/agriculture/other-agri...).

C++ and Python software engineers - https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/careers/software-engineer-2.html

ML/AI Engineering - https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/careers/software-engineer-machin...

User Interface - https://www.nrec.ri.cmu.edu/careers/user-interface-software-...

We've built profitable travel businesses in the past, and at Wanderlog, we try to take the best parts of each of the our past workplaces and bring them together.

We believe in work-life balance. We work regular hours, take time off as a team to eat lunch together (and even cook!), exercise, and enjoy time with friends and family. We love travel and believe it rejuvenates us and makes us better people, and have quarterly travel offsites where the goal is to just enjoy visiting a new place and use the tools we’ve built.

If you enjoy travel, and would love to make it easier for the rest of the world to do it, send us a note at founders@wanderlog.com! We’d love for you to join our team.

children.author: rjyoungling
children.text: Well, generally speaking, HN culture frowns upon low-value comments. That doesn't just imply negative comments but also '+1' type comments. Which is part of the reason why threads on HN are of significantly higher quality than those on other platforms.

children.author: DoreenMichele
children.text:
It looks to me like no actual rule was broken per se, but GP is aware he was breaking more like a thing of etiquette. It's kind of an "apologies in advance, as I know this is sort of rude, but I'm going to say it anyway because I'm saying something nice" that wasn't phrased optimally.

HN generally discourages lightweight chit chat to protect the signal to noise ratio. They more strongly discourage it in these Hiring posts and it seems to me that's the correct way to handle it because this is intended as a free advertising space, not a discussion space.

In part for purposes of making advertisers comfortable posting here so they will post at all, HN more strictly forbids attacks against the advertisers because that would drive away a lot of advertisers and harm the utility of these posts. But, also, these posts have a lot of little ads and it's already a huge pile of info to sort through if you are job hunting, even without chit chat and ugly, long tangents thrown in.

HN likely doesn't have the manpower to lock these threads and institute a pre approval process as the mechanism that protects these posts as 99% (free) ads. So they rely on certain social expectations to make this work.

Since the membership very much values these posts, the membership generally does a good job of respecting certain expectations.

There are spaces on the internet where the meme is "This is why we can't have nice things" and it typically gets stated as a way to say "It's not the fault of incompetent moderation. No, the members are just assholes who won't behave." (Often stated by the mods, who are incompetent and prone to putting out the fire with gasoline.)

HN has both competent moderation and members who more or less try hard to behave. This is why we can have nice things around here, like the Who is Hiring threads, which are a free service benefiting both businesses in need of staff and people in need of employment.
out of curiosity, what HN law are you potentially breaking? I'm guessing there's a law that prohibits posts that simply say another comment is good?

children.author: dang
rjyoungling
children.text: No, I totally get it! I didn't mean to accidentally imply that you were being unreasonable. I was merely being facetious about HN culture my friend!

If you mean the rule at the top, it's not up there to prevent comments like this, but rather the complaints that people sometimes post about their previous opinions/experiences with a company in reply to a job posting. We don't allow those because we don't have any way of knowing which are justified and which aren't. Bad corporate behavior is a thing,  disgruntled commenters are a thing (the kind who are good at telling only one misleading side of the story), and the two can be hard to tell apart. Sometimes the community can sort things out through the informal adjudication process that arises in HN threads around controversial questions—but those are lengthy and Who Is Hiring threads are not the place for it.
I'm risking my behind here by breaking HN law but I just had to say, this is some very strong copywriting assuming you're technical. Excellent job man. Good luck!

Khan Academy | Mountain View, CA and REMOTE USA/CANADA | Senior Backend / Fullstack | https://khanacademy.org/careers

We're a non-profit with a mission to provide a free, world-class education to anyone, anywhere. It's a big mission that we're taking on step by step. While we want anyone to be able to get a great education independently, we've been focusing a lot on trying to help teachers working in their classrooms (and a lot of teachers and parents are using Khan away from their classrooms right now!)

Our site has been built on Python 2 and Google App Engine for its first 10 years of existence. We're now in the midst of a rebuild in Go (still on App Engine).[1] Parts of that new Go-based infrastructure are already running in production.

To say that this is an exciting time for us would be an understatement, I think, but we continue to have working sustainably as an engineering principle. (Our principles are available publicly[2].)

children.text: Shorter - 2-3 sentences. Less is more : ).
I'd appreciate from the downvoters how I can improve.

I'm a CS grad with some work experience (1 year dev, 1 year coding bootcamp teacher). See me as a junior that ramps up quicker than the average junior (e.g. last month I owned a lot of boxes at hackthebox.eu for fun and was a top 5% after 2 weeks of non-stop playing [1]).

I wrote my thesis related to Engelbard. So I think we have a cultural click. Which is why I'm writing all this.

The reason I'm not applying but simply writing things here is because I'm tired of applying (it's hard to hear more than 100+ "no" while at university you were a top student). But I do want to know if you guys think I'm worth considering.

Which is why I'm brutally honest with the following:

Companies tend to reject me due to lack of experience, and (in my opinion) undervalue how quick I can pick things up and how willing I am to work amazingly hard, especially at the beginning of a job. When they hire me they tend to be surprised with how wrong they were about me.

My strength is that I'm a generalist, much more so than most people. My weakness is that people have the perception that I can't be a specialist. But anyone that gave me a chance in hiring me during my freelance time know that I am capable of performing one role as a specialist (full-stack developer with a business and security mindset).

During my good days I tend to have an Elon Musk mindset. He says that working 80 to 100 hours per week means you learn 2 to 2.5 times faster, I mostly agree -- I think it is sometimes more because the interconnectness of things pushes the multiple a bit higher. During my bad days I simply want to work 40 hours per week go home and relax. During these times I sort of don't want to work due to stress, but know that I have to work because it keeps my mind sharp.

[1] I was in "Elon Musk" mode for a month.

raw.excerpt: About the Team/RoleWe are looking for a highly entrepreneurial Principal Data Scientist with deep payments expertise to help define and build the next generation of intelligent payment products.
raw.description:
About the Team/Role

We are looking for a highly entrepreneurial Principal Data Scientist with deep payments expertise to help define and build the next generation of intelligent payment products. This individual will combine hands-on data science, machine learning, payment-domain expertise, and strong product instincts to identify high-value opportunities hidden within corporate payments data and turn them into production-ready intelligence. This is not a traditional analytics or reporting role. The successful candidate will start with ambiguous business problems, explore data, form hypotheses, build models and signals, and partner with Product and Engineering to turn insights into scalable capabilities. The role offers near-greenfield opportunity and end-to-end ownership within Corporate Payments, with a focus on revenue growth and measurable business value.


The initial focus includes exploring opportunities such as BIN routing optimization, where small improvements across high transaction volumes may create significant net benefit, as well as supplier onboarding, customer acquisition, and identifying suppliers that already accept card payments and could be connected to WEX customers. Over time, this work can help establish a trusted intelligence foundation for future AI agents and agentic payment experiences.


What You’ll Do:

  • Discover high-value payment opportunities by combining deep payments knowledge with exploratory data science and machine learning.
  • Use corporate payments data to identify opportunities for revenue growth, improved payment economics, supplier onboarding, and new customer acquisition; identify additional data that could unlock further analysis.
  • Build intelligent payment data products that move beyond dashboards to predictions, recommendations, optimization, and decisioning.
  • Develop models and signals related to merchant and supplier behavior, payment acceptance, authorization performance, BIN/interchange optimization, payment routing, fraud/risk, and payment economics.
  • Create connected intelligence across customers, suppliers, merchants, transactions, payment methods, networks, and other payment entities.
  • Identify patterns in large-scale transaction data that can improve acceptance, payment performance, revenue, and margin; form hypotheses and prove value with rigorous analysis.
  • Prototype quickly using Python, SQL, machine learning, and modern data platforms to demonstrate value before scaling solutions.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering to productionize models, signals, and decisioning capabilities.
  • Design experimentation and measurement frameworks to demonstrate the incremental business value of models and recommendations.
  • Help define the semantic and contextual intelligence needed for future payments AI agents and agentic experiences.
  • Act as a thought partner to Payments leadership, proactively identifying opportunities rather than waiting for fully defined requirements.
  • Mentor data analysts and collaborate with data scientists across the broader organization, sharing practices and raising the technical and data-science bar.

What You Bring:

  • 10+ years of relevant experience in data science or a related quantitative discipline, including hands-on work building production machine-learning, predictive, optimization, or decisioning solutions.
  • Deep subject-matter expertise in payments, credit cards, payment transactions, or payment infrastructure. Strong domain understanding is essential; technical ability alone is not sufficient.
  • Experience in several relevant areas such as authorization, acceptance, interchange, BINs, merchant behavior, payment routing, fraud/risk, transaction economics, settlement, or payment-network dynamics.
  • Strong Python and SQL skills and experience working with large-scale transactional datasets. Able to move between exploratory analysis, feature engineering, modeling, experimentation, and productionization.
  • Ability to understand not only what happened in payment data, but why it happened and what the business could do differently.
  • A builder and entrepreneurial mindset: able to independently identify an opportunity, explore data, test a hypothesis, prototype a solution, and develop a business case without requiring a fully defined roadmap.
  • Strong product instincts and judgment to distinguish technically interesting work from work that creates measurable business value.
  • Ability to work directly with Product, Engineering, Commercial, Risk, and business leaders and to communicate clearly and succinctly with director- and VP-level stakeholders.
  • Customer empathy, proactive collaboration and sharing of learnings, accountability to lead by example, and willingness to challenge existing approaches constructively.
  • Established technical leadership and a collaborative approach to mentoring others while remaining open to learning from peers.

Nice to Have:

  • Advanced degree (master’s degree or above) in Data Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Operations Research, Economics, or another quantitative discipline. Equivalent depth demonstrated through experience may be considered on a case by case basis.
  • Experience with R and modern data platforms such as Snowflake or Databricks. Python and SQL are required; SAS alone is not sufficient.
  • Experience at a major card network, card company, payment processor, transaction-focused fintech, or financial institution.
  • Curiosity about GenAI and agentic systems and interest in designing intelligence that can ultimately be consumed by AI agents.

Why This Role Matters

Corporate Payments has an opportunity to unlock meaningful revenue and net benefit from data that has recently become available. This role will lead the discovery and validation of those opportunities, including payment-routing and interchange economics, supplier connectivity, and customer growth. The successful candidate will have the autonomy to build a portfolio of high-value work, influence business decisions with evidence, and help establish scalable intelligence capabilities for future payment products and agentic experiences. As the portfolio grows, there may be an opportunity to build a supporting team over time; direct people management is not part of the initial role, and continued individual-contributor growth is also supported.


The base pay range represents the anticipated low and high end of the pay range for this position. Actual pay rates will vary and will be based on various factors, such as your qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role. Base pay is one component of WEX's total compensation package. Most sales positions are eligible for commission under the terms of an applicable plan. Non-sales roles are typically eligible for a quarterly or annual bonus based on their role and applicable plan. WEX's comprehensive and market competitive benefits are designed to support your personal and professional well-being. Benefits include health, dental and vision insurances, retirement savings plan, paid time off, health savings account, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, disability insurance, tuition reimbursement, and more. For more information, check out the "About Us" section.Pay Range: $215,000.00 - $243,800.00
